A2A-01.statement: The agent card is generated from the catalog.

A2A-02.statement: Every applicable operation has one skill.

A2A-03.statement: A skill carries the operation ID and its input/output modes.

A2A-04.statement: A skill marked not applicable states a reason in the catalog.

A2A-05.statement: An A2A task maps to one operation invocation.

A2A-06.statement: A2A task state is stored only in `TaskStore`, never in business tables.

A2A-07.statement: Business state is read and written only through operations.

A2A-08.statement: The adapter converts A2A messages to operation requests and back.

A2A-09.statement: The adapter contains no business logic.

A2A-10.statement: Task cancellation maps to operation cancellation only when the operation supports it; otherwise it returns the operation's conflict/state result.

A2A-11.statement: The adopted A2A security scheme is implemented as declared in the agent card.

A2A-12.statement: Tokens are verified by the shared verifier with the A2A audience.

A2A-13.statement: A token for another interface is rejected.

A2A-14.statement: The adapter does not authorize the target; the operation does.

A2A-15.statement: Secrets and tokens are not written to task state, logs, or errors.

A2A-16.statement: Task updates use the A2A-defined event model, not an ad-hoc envelope.

A2A-17.statement: Streaming termination distinguishes success, failure, and cancellation.

A2A-18.statement: Every operation category has an A2A error mapping.

A2A-19.statement: Error details never contain tokens, secrets, or raw provider responses.

A2A-20.statement: Every task is bound to a `TaskOwner` (subject and tenant); load/save require the owner.

A2A-21.statement: The adapter authorizes protocol-owned task get/cancel/subscribe against the owner; business authorization stays in the operation.

A2A-22.statement: Protocol errors and business execution errors are mapped separately.

A2A-23.statement: `A2aConfig` MUST record the adopted protocol version, transport profile, and capabilities, and MUST declare a binding for the selected profile that fixes operation-to-skill or message selection, success and failure representation, correlation location, and lifecycle mapping.

A2A-24.statement: Every task artifact MUST carry the operation's `request_id` in the location declared by the selected A2A binding.

A2A-25.statement: A2A send and stream methods MUST use one shared executor and SDK wire framing.

A2A-26.statement: Production A2A task state, execution claims, idempotency records, and event logs MUST survive instance replacement.

A2A-27.statement: Every task, cancellation, and replay access MUST bind subject and tenant at the persistence boundary.

A2A-28.statement: A2A `message/send` and `message/stream` MUST share the same operation invocation and terminal semantics.

A2A-29.statement: A2A cancellation, disconnect, and resubscribe MUST be distinct and MUST use durable event cursors.

A2A-30.statement: A2A auth and agent card MUST declare and enforce the configured security scheme and audience.

APP-01.statement: A project MUST declare its profiles and MUST list every unimplemented interface as absent.

APP-02.statement: A project MUST maintain an operation catalog using the §11 template.

APP-03.statement: A project MUST map its crates to §3.1 roles and record the mapping.

APP-04.statement: Exceptions MUST be declared with a reason, scope, owner, and expiry. Undeclared exceptions are defects.

APP-05.statement: This document is versioned. A project pins the version it applies.

APP-06.statement: Adoption order SHOULD, within the interface profiles a project selects, be: identity-core and identity-jwt → operation authorization and conformance → REST → WebSocket → CLI → gRPC → MCP → A2A. A project MAY select any subset.

APP-07.statement: Each adopted rule MUST first have a failing conformance test, then an implementation, then a refactor.

ARC-01.statement: Each crate MUST have one primary runtime role from §3.1. Additional roles (`tooling`, `test-support`, `build-support`, `utility`) are allowed when declared in `RULES-PROFILE.toml` with their allowed dependency edges. A crate MUST NOT mix incompatible runtime roles.

ARC-03.statement: `*-core` and `*-operation` MUST NOT depend on `axum`, `tonic`, `rmcp`, `a2a-*`, `clap`, or any protocol SDK.

ARC-04.statement: An interface crate MUST NOT depend on another interface crate.

ARC-05.statement: `*-conformance` MAY depend on every public boundary; no runtime crate may depend on `*-conformance`.

ARC-06.statement: Only the assembly/binary MAY depend on concrete authentication implementations (`identity-jwt`, `identity-local`, `identity-sso`) and wire them together.

ARC-07.statement: `*-core` MUST define ports (traits) for external effects; it MUST NOT call infrastructure directly.

ARC-08.statement: `*-operation` MUST depend on `identity-core` traits, never on `identity-jwt` or `identity-sso`.

ARC-09.statement: Crate names MUST use the project prefix and the role suffix (`<project-c>-core`, `<project-c>-operation`, `<project-c>-rest`, and so on).

ARC-10.statement: Inside a crate, modules SHOULD follow `api/`, `model/`, `state/`, `error/`, `security/`, `config/`, `tests/`.

AUTH-01.statement: Token verification MUST be expressed as a protocol-independent `AccessTokenVerifier` trait in `identity-core`.

AUTH-02.statement: Token issuance MUST be expressed as a `TokenIssuer` trait; every login method MUST use this single issuance path.

AUTH-03.statement: Access tokens MUST be JWS. JWE is not used.

AUTH-04.statement: The default signing algorithm MUST be asymmetric (`EdDSA` or `ES256`). HS256 is allowed only under the `local-only` profile.

AUTH-05.statement: The verifier MUST enforce an explicit algorithm allowlist and MUST reject `none`, unknown algorithms, and algorithm/operation mismatches.

AUTH-06.statement: Tokens MUST contain `iss`, `sub`, `aud`, `exp`, `iat`, and `jti`. `nbf` and `scope` MAY be present.

AUTH-08.statement: `aud` MUST identify one interface or resource. Wildcard audiences are forbidden. A token for one interface MUST be rejected by another.

AUTH-09.statement: Access-token lifetime MUST be short and configurable (recommended 5–15 minutes).

AUTH-10.statement: Verification keys MUST be resolved through a `KeyStore` keyed by `kid`. Multiple active public keys MUST be supported for rotation.

AUTH-11.statement: Key material MUST NOT be fetched from `jku`, `x5u`, or any URL carried by the token. JWKS URLs MUST be fixed by configuration.

AUTH-12.statement: Validation order MUST be: algorithm allowlist → signature → `iss` → `aud` → `exp`/`nbf` → `typ` → `sub` → tenant/delegation → `ver` → `jti`.

AUTH-13.statement: Access tokens, ID tokens, and other token types MUST be mutually exclusive by `typ`, required claims, key, and audience. An external ID token MUST NOT be accepted as an access token.

AUTH-14.statement: Revocation MUST be checked after signature validation, using `jti` and/or a user-level token version. Revocation checks MUST NOT replace cryptographic validation.

AUTH-15.statement: Refresh tokens MUST be opaque random values, stored only as hashes, rotated on every use, and revoked as a session family on reuse detection.

AUTH-16.statement: Auth failures exposed to clients MUST collapse to 401 or 403. Detailed reasons MUST be logged, never returned.

AUTH-17.statement: Secrets, tokens, authorization codes, verifiers, and passwords MUST NOT appear in logs, `Debug`, error bodies, or metrics.

AUTH-18.statement: Login MUST be an operation (`auth.token.issue` or equivalent). It MUST NOT be a transport-specific router contract in `identity-core`.

AUTH-19.statement: Each interface MAY implement its own credential acquisition flow, but all flows MUST end at the same `TokenIssuer`.

AUTH-20.statement: HS256 is permitted only when all of the following hold: single process, no cross-interface token use, explicit `local-only` profile, key length ≥ 32 bytes.

AUTH-21.statement: REST MUST accept only `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Other schemes, multiple headers, and empty tokens MUST return 401.

AUTH-22.statement: WebSocket MUST use a short-lived, single-use, client-bound one-time ticket. Long-lived JWT query parameters are forbidden.

AUTH-23.statement: gRPC MUST read credentials from metadata and map auth failures to `UNAUTHENTICATED` or `PERMISSION_DENIED`.

AUTH-24.statement: CLI MUST store tokens in an OS-protected store or a `0600` file, never in argv or shell history.

AUTH-25.statement: CLI local execution MUST establish an explicit principal and MUST NOT grant implicit administrator rights.

AUTH-26.statement: MCP MUST implement the authentication discovery/challenge required by the adopted MCP specification, and MUST NOT pass a received token through to a downstream API.

AUTH-27.statement: A2A MUST implement the security mechanism required by the adopted A2A specification.

AUTH-28.statement: Authentication requirement (`Required`/`Anonymous`) MUST be separate from scope. Anonymous operations use `AnonymousOperation` and never receive a `VerifiedIdentity`.

AUTH-29.statement: `VerifiedIdentity` MUST carry the credential binding: interface, audience, method, authentication time, expiry, token ID, and token version. The dispatcher MUST reject a binding mismatch.

AUTH-30.statement: A session ticket and a local identity issuer MUST create a new binding. A token or identity verified for one interface/audience MUST NOT be reused for another.

AUTH-31.statement: Delegation MUST preserve `actor` and `on_behalf_of`, and the verifier MUST reject an unauthorized actor or an excessive scope set.

AUTHZ-01.statement: Authorization MUST be expressed as `Authorizer::require(identity, action, resource)`.

AUTHZ-02.statement: Scope is necessary but never sufficient. Ownership, tenant, and resource state MUST also be checked.

AUTHZ-03.statement: Tenant and owner checks MUST use the identity and the loaded resource, not request-supplied IDs.

AUTHZ-04.statement: Anonymous operations MUST be explicitly declared. `Option<Identity>` must not be used to express "maybe anonymous".

AUTHZ-05.statement: A target in another tenant MUST return not-found. A target in the caller's tenant with insufficient rights MUST return permission-denied.

AUTHZ-06.statement: Scope strings MUST NOT be compared in handlers or adapters; policy belongs in one authorizer implementation.

AUTHZ-07.statement: Authorization and mutation races MUST be handled with a transaction or a conditional update.

AUTHZ-08.statement: An interface-level pre-check MAY exist, but it MUST NOT replace the operation-level authorization.

AUTHZ-09.statement: The same identity, action, and resource MUST produce the same authorization result through every interface.

BP-01.statement: This blueprint is the mandatory implementation method for validation and documentation. An alternate method requires a versioned exception.

BP-02.statement: Every request type uses `#[contract::input]` and implements `ContractValidate`.

BP-03.statement: The macro emits the validator, descriptor, schema registration, and inventory entries described in §3.

BP-04.statement: `Operation::Request` has a `ContractValidate` bound. `validate_json` runs before the idempotency claim; `prepare_validated` runs only on the acquired branch; replay calls `replay_authorize` only.

BP-05.statement: `validation-contract` owns the runtime types and `inventory` registrations in §2.

BP-06.statement: Rule parameters are const-friendly and serialized to the exact JSON format in §4.2.

BP-07.statement: `*-docgen` provides the four subcommands in §4.1 and depends on the operation crate to link registrations.

BP-08.statement: The schema registry is authoritative for all interfaces; `utoipa` output is compared, not used as the only source.

BP-09.statement: Completeness, English, secrets, and determinism checks follow §4.4 and the exit codes.

BP-10.statement: Generated documentation is written atomically and sorted deterministically.

BP-12.statement: Custom rules require `id`, `check`, `fields`, `description`, and `code`; conditional rules require `when`.

BP-13.statement: Unknown or type-incompatible rules fail compilation with a span.

BP-14.statement: No adapter implements interface-specific input validation.

BP-15.statement: Documentation is English-only; non-English prose fails the English check.

BP-16.statement: Documentation and examples contain no secrets.

BP-18.statement: REST is not required for schema dump or docgen; a non-REST project uses the same subcommands.

BP-19.statement: Generated files carry the generated marker and are never hand-edited.

BP-20.statement: A feature that cannot follow the blueprint requires an amendment to this document, not a project fork.

CLI-01.statement: Argument types are generated separately from operation types. Clap attributes never appear on operation structs.

CLI-02.statement: Every catalog operation has one subcommand.

CLI-03.statement: A composition command is allowed only when documented and mapped to a sequence of operations.

CLI-04.statement: The command converts arguments into the operation request and calls the dispatcher.

CLI-05.statement: Data goes to stdout; progress and diagnostics go to stderr.

CLI-06.statement: `--json` emits one JSON value; `--jsonl` emits one JSON object per line.

CLI-07.statement: Human output is not parsed by scripts; JSON is the machine contract.

CLI-08.statement: Exit codes follow the fixed table.

CLI-09.statement: Secrets are read from a file, stdin, or TTY.

CLI-10.statement: A secret in argv is rejected before any operation.

CLI-11.statement: Secrets are never written to stdout, logs, or error messages.

CLI-12.statement: Token files are checked for restrictive permissions.

CLI-14.statement: The remote client is a protocol client, not an interface-adapter dependency.

CLI-15.statement: clap parsing types MUST be generated inside the CLI adapter and MUST NOT annotate operation-domain types.

CLI-16.statement: The CLI MUST reject argv credential contents and MUST read secrets only from approved file, stdin, or TTY sources.

CLI-17.statement: The CLI MUST reserve stdout for results and MUST use the fixed exit-code table for every termination path.

CONF-01.statement: Every catalog operation appears in the matrix.

CONF-02.statement: Every implemented interface has a driver.

CONF-03.statement: Every cell is required or not applicable with a reason.

CONF-04.statement: A profile absent from `RULES-PROFILE.toml` is not a non-applicable cell.

CONF-05.statement: Every case names a fixture with setup and reset.

CONF-06.statement: IDs and time are deterministic in fixtures.

CONF-07.statement: Generated IDs and timestamps use semantic matchers, not exact equality.

CONF-08.statement: A case must not depend on the order of another case.

CONF-09.statement: A mutation case must assert the resulting state, not only the response.

CONF-10.statement: Expected results are derived from the operation specification, not from one interface.

CONF-11.statement: All interfaces answering the same wrong result is a failure.

CONF-12.statement: The oracle covers normal, failure, state, authorization, idempotency, and streaming.

CONF-13.statement: Every required interface rejects a token for another audience.

CONF-14.statement: An identity with a mismatched interface or audience binding is rejected.

CONF-15.statement: An expired binding is rejected even when the signature is valid.

CONF-16.statement: A session ticket creates a new binding; the ticket redemption deadline and connection expiry are distinct.

CONF-17.statement: Delegation preserves `actor` and `on_behalf_of` and rejects unauthorized delegation.

CONF-18.statement: Negative authentication cases include missing claims, future `nbf`, wrong claim types, token version mismatch, and revocation.

CONF-19.statement: No interface can bypass operation authorization.

CONF-21.statement: The trusted constructor is not reachable from adapter crates; allowed call sites are audited.

CONF-22.statement: A compile-fail test is not treated as a general proof of non-bypass.

CONF-23.statement: Protocol-owned resources (WS subscriptions, A2A tasks, MCP sessions) are authorized by the adapter; business resources are not.

CONF-24.statement: Concurrent claims for the same namespace and key MUST produce one execution.

CONF-25.statement: A replay MUST re-authorize the current caller before returning the stored result. A re-authorization failure MUST return an authorization error and MUST NOT execute `prepare` or `execute`.

CONF-26.statement: The same key with a different canonical request hash MUST return a conflict.

CONF-27.statement: A crash after business commit but before publication is recovered; the event is not lost.

CONF-28.statement: Irreversible effects follow the declared recovery policy.

CONF-29.statement: No unrelated external API wait occurs inside a database transaction; transaction-required DB communication is allowed.

CONF-30.statement: Server stream items, EOF, error, and cancel match the operation contract.

CONF-31.statement: Client stream input, EOF, and cancel match the contract.

CONF-32.statement: Bidi streams preserve independent half-close and cancellation.

CONF-34.statement: A cancelled operation's result is queryable through the authorized result lookup when the catalog declares it; a bare request ID is insufficient.

CONF-35.statement: TLS, real upgrade, and CLI process boundaries are covered out-of-process.

CONF-36.statement: A driver that cannot exercise a required boundary reports `Fail`, not `NotApplicable`.

CONF-37.statement: The crate graph passes the forbidden-edge checks.

CONF-38.statement: Every rule ID in the registry has a verdict.

CONF-39.statement: A missing verification is a failure, not a skip.

CONF-40.statement: Documentation, file existence, and fixture names are not proof.

CONF-41.statement: The report names every failed row and every rule without evidence.

CONF-42.statement: After SSO is added, existing operation signatures, subject IDs, and business data references are unchanged.

CONF-43.statement: An external ID token is rejected as an access token on every interface.

CONF-44.statement: An internal access token is rejected as an external ID token.

CONF-45.statement: A stream started through an adapter reaches the Dispatcher stream API and delivers items, EOF, and cancel.

CONF-46.statement: An expired lease owner MUST NOT complete or commit after a new owner acquires the claim.

CONF-47.statement: A replay after a successful delete, create, or approve MUST return the stored result with current authorization, not a state-precondition error, only when the current caller is authorized.

CONF-48.statement: Same-transaction completion, business mutation, authorized target, and outbox intent MUST be atomic; a rollback leaves none of them, and a crash after commit recovers both the result and the event.

CONF-49.statement: REST merges body context and header context, rejects conflicts, and returns `request_id` on success and on every failure path.

CONF-50.statement: A long-lived WebSocket connection observes revocation within the configured maximum staleness.

CONF-51.statement: Result lookup is authorized by the recorded subject, tenant, or an authorized operator; a bare request ID is insufficient.

CONF-52.statement: Refresh consumes the current generation and creates the next generation in one transaction; family history and reuse behavior match the declared policy.

CONF-53.statement: Every implemented interface has generated documentation and every applicable operation has a section.

CONF-54.statement: Documentation completeness, English-only, and secret-free gates pass.

CONF-55.statement: Documentation generation is deterministic for the same inputs and version.

CONF-56.statement: A project without the REST profile still generates documentation for its implemented interfaces.

CONF-57.statement: Every request uses the generated validator, and the same input produces the same validation result through every interface.

CONF-58.statement: Standard constraints map to schema keywords; byte-length and non-ECMA regex rules are custom and not mis-mapped.

CONF-59.statement: Every custom rule has `id`, `check`, `fields`, `description`, and `code`, and appears in every applicable interface reference.

CONF-60.statement: Unknown or type-incompatible rules fail compilation; no rule is silently omitted.

CONF-61.statement: Every request uses the macro; the validator, descriptor, schema registration, and inventory entries are present.

CONF-62.statement: `*-docgen` implements the four subcommands and both registry dumps; the operation crate is linked.

CONF-63.statement: Completeness, English, secret, and determinism checks match the blueprint and exit codes.

CONF-64.statement: No alternate validation/documentation method is used without a versioned exception.

CONF-65.statement: Generated validation MUST run before the idempotency claim for both replay and new requests; replay MUST call `replay_authorize` and MUST NOT call `prepare` or `execute`.

CONF-66.statement: A claim whose authorization target is not finalized MUST NOT return a stored result.

CONF-67.statement: For each implemented profile, conformance MUST verify that the representation conforms to the protocol and maps to the common invocation and result model. Byte equality across protocols MUST NOT be required.

CORE-01.statement: Every aggregate with a lifecycle has one root type and one state enum. Value objects and stateless aggregates are exempt.

CORE-02.statement: Illegal states are unrepresentable. A state transition returns `Result<NextState, DomainError>`.

CORE-04.statement: IDs are typed newtypes; a raw `u64` or `Uuid` is not used as an entity ID across boundaries.

CORE-05.statement: Time is injected through `Clock`; `Utc::now()` is forbidden in core.

CORE-06.statement: Randomness and ID allocation go through `IdGenerator`.

CORE-07.statement: Domain errors are typed and carry a stable code.

CORE-09.statement: Core does not serialize wire envelopes or know protocol status codes.

CORE-10.statement: Domain events are values; publication happens outside core.

DOC-01.statement: Every implemented interface MUST have generated usage documentation.

DOC-02.statement: The operation catalog is the authoritative operation list and binding map.

DOC-03.statement: The generator MUST consume a neutral schema registry, not parse Rust source.

DOC-04.statement: `utoipa`/OpenAPI MAY be used as a schema source and REST output, but MUST NOT be the only source for non-REST interfaces.

DOC-05.statement: Interface-specific documentation MUST come from interface bindings, not be inferred from REST.

DOC-06.statement: Documentation generation MUST NOT require a running REST server or REST adapter.

DOC-07.statement: Every operation section MUST include schema, examples, auth, errors, idempotency, streaming, authorization, and conformance ID.

DOC-08.statement: Every implemented interface MUST have a reference section for every applicable operation.

DOC-09.statement: OpenAPI and Swagger UI MUST be generated from the same schema registry as the other references.

DOC-10.statement: A missing operation, interface, field, error category, auth statement, or example MUST fail the build.

DOC-11.statement: Generated documentation MUST be English-only; a non-English string fails the build.

DOC-12.statement: Generation MUST be deterministic for the same inputs and version.

DOC-13.statement: Documentation and examples MUST NOT contain secrets, tokens, or passwords.

DOC-14.statement: Documentation MUST record `spec_version` and the input digest.

DOC-15.statement: Documentation generation MUST be part of CI/conformance; a missing artifact fails the gate.

DOC-16.statement: Input constraints MUST be documented from the `ValidationDescriptor`, not from a hand-written list or inferred code.

DOC-17.statement: Custom validation rules MUST appear as readable English text in every applicable interface reference.

DOC-18.statement: Interface documentation and conformance MUST read the binding declaration as the source of truth for protocol version, transport, capabilities, correlation location, and lifecycle mapping; one SDK or correlation location MUST NOT be imposed across profiles.

DOC-19.statement: Rule ranges in index sections MUST be generated from the rule registry. Hand-written ranges MUST NOT be used; the index MUST reference Part III.12 and Part III.15 instead of duplicating their ranges.

ERR-01.statement: Operations MUST return a protocol-independent error value with `code`, `domain`, `retryable`, and optional structured details.

ERR-02.statement: Error codes MUST be stable identifiers; adapters MUST map them to protocol statuses.

ERR-03.statement: Error values MUST NOT contain secrets, tokens, passwords, or raw provider responses.

ERR-04.statement: Retryability MUST be explicit. Validation and authentication errors are not retryable.

ERR-05.statement: Each interface MUST have one error-mapping table and one test per code.

FREE-01.statement: A rule MUST NOT enumerate a closed set of operations, scopes, error codes, features, or domain types.

FREE-02.statement: A project MAY add operations, scopes, error codes, auth methods, interfaces, streaming modes, and storage without changing this ruleset.

FREE-03.statement: A project MAY use any algorithm, data structure, crate, or optimization behind a port, provided conformance passes.

FREE-04.statement: A project MAY implement a subset of interface profiles; absence must be declared, not inferred.

FREE-05.statement: A project MAY add a project-local extension crate implementing the declared extension traits. The extension MUST pass conformance.

FREE-06.statement: If a shared contract blocks a legitimate feature, the contract is extended with a new default method, trait, feature flag, or version. The project MUST NOT fork the contract.

FREE-07.statement: A rule that limits a feature without protecting a seam or invariant is a defect in the ruleset and MUST be amended.

FREE-08.statement: Rule amendments follow the versioning policy in §9; existing projects are never broken silently.

FREE-09.statement: A project MAY add crate roles for tooling, tests, benchmarks, build support, or utility code. The role and its allowed dependency edges are declared; forbidden edges still apply.

FREE-10.statement: A state-machine requirement applies only to aggregates with a lifecycle. Value objects and stateless aggregates are not forced into a state enum.

FREE-11.statement: Resource identifiers are open. UUID, content hash, and composite keys are all valid behind `ResourceId`.

FREE-12.statement: Interface adoption order is a recommendation, not a precondition. A project MAY implement any subset, including MCP or A2A alone.

FREE-13.statement: Only public module boundaries, generated files, and forbidden edges are fixed. Hand-written internal layout may differ.

FREE-14.statement: A contract MUST define the responsibilities, observable guarantees, and verification conditions at its shared boundary. It MUST NOT prescribe implementation choices that do not affect those guarantees.

FREE-15.statement: Implementers MUST resolve unspecified details, ambiguities, and local inconsistencies using rule precedence, design intent, compatibility requirements, and safety invariants, and MUST carry the resolution through implementation and verification. The resolution SHOULD change the fewest shared guarantees and preserve legitimate extension points.

FREE-16.statement: Where a choice affects interoperability within a declared profile, the profile or binding MUST specify that choice. Otherwise, conforming implementations MAY differ.

GRPC-01.statement: The proto is generated from the catalog and checked in.

GRPC-02.statement: Field numbers are never reused. Removed numbers are `reserved`.

GRPC-03.statement: Scalars that need presence are declared `optional`.

GRPC-04.statement: `Context` uses the fixed field numbers from Part III.2 §8.1.

GRPC-05.statement: Generated protobuf types do not appear in `*-core` or `*-operation`.

GRPC-06.statement: Credentials come from gRPC metadata, not from the message body.

GRPC-07.statement: Missing, malformed, or wrong-audience tokens return `UNAUTHENTICATED`.

GRPC-09.statement: The interceptor does not authorize the target; the operation does.

GRPC-10.statement: Every category maps to the status above.

GRPC-11.statement: Rich details are encoded as `google.rpc.Status` details or the JSON detail field; they never contain secrets.

GRPC-12.statement: The request deadline is propagated into `WireContext`.

GRPC-13.statement: `U` maps to unary; `S`, `C`, `B` map to the corresponding stream.

GRPC-14.statement: Client cancellation cancels the operation when the operation supports it; otherwise the result is queryable by request ID.

GRPC-15.statement: Message size and keepalive limits are configured.

GRPC-16.statement: Transport uses TLS outside loopback-only local mode.

GRPC-17.statement: Every reply message carries the operation's `request_id`.

GRPC-18.statement: Typed protobuf messages are the gRPC binding; the universal JSON-bytes envelope is not required.

GRPC-19.statement: A cancelled operation's result is queryable through the authorized result lookup when the catalog declares it; a bare request ID is insufficient.

GRPC-20.statement: gRPC services MUST implement generated tonic traits and MUST keep protobuf types outside core and operation contracts.

GRPC-21.statement: Every gRPC streaming shape MUST propagate deadlines, input half-close, and cancellation to the matching dispatcher stream method.

GRPC-22.statement: Non-loopback gRPC exposure MUST use the declared TLS boundary and shared redacted status mapping.

ID-01.statement: `SubjectId` MUST be an internal, immutable identifier. Email addresses and external provider IDs MUST NOT be used as `sub`.

ID-02.statement: Operations MUST receive exactly one identity type: `VerifiedIdentity`. A duplicate `Principal` type is forbidden.

ID-03.statement: `VerifiedIdentity` MUST be constructible only by the verifier. Fields MUST be private; the constructor MUST be `pub(crate)` or equivalent.

ID-04.statement: `VerifiedIdentity` MUST NOT implement `Deserialize` or any public constructor.

ID-05.statement: Delegated execution MUST distinguish the actor from the subject: `actor` and `on_behalf_of` MUST be separate fields.

ID-06.statement: Operations MUST NOT receive a raw JWT, `iss`, external account ID, or provider name.

IDN-07.statement: Refresh tokens are opaque random values, not JWTs.

IDN-09.statement: Every use consumes and rotates the token atomically.

IDN-10.statement: Reuse of a consumed token revokes the session family.

IDN-11.statement: Sessions are independent of the login method.

IDN-12.statement: `users.token_version` is included in claims as `ver` and checked.

IDN-13.statement: Consume and next-generation insert happen in one transaction; `(family_id, generation)` is unique.

IDN-14.statement: The loser of concurrent refresh receives `invalid_grant`; idempotent grace requires an encrypted replacement cache, not a hash-only record.

IDN-16.statement: OIDC uses Authorization Code + PKCE S256.

IDN-20.statement: External ID tokens are discarded after verification.

IDN-21.statement: SSO output is `AuthenticatedUser`; `TokenIssuer` issues the internal token.

IF-01.statement: An adapter MUST only: extract credentials, convert input, call the verifier, call the operation, convert output, and map errors.

IF-02.statement: An adapter MUST NOT implement business rules, authorization policy, or persistence.

IF-03.statement: Credential extraction MUST be adapter-specific; verification MUST call the shared `AccessTokenVerifier`.

IF-04.statement: Protocol errors MUST be mapped from the protocol-independent error vocabulary. Adapters MUST NOT invent operation errors.

IF-05.statement: Every implemented interface MUST expose every operation unless the operation is explicitly declared not applicable, with a reason.

IF-06.statement: No interface may call another interface to reach an operation.

IF-07.statement: Protocol state (connection, subscription, task, stream) MUST remain in the adapter or in `*-operation` state, never duplicated in both.

IF-08.statement: Every operation response MUST carry the operation's `request_id`; streaming messages MUST carry a correlation identifier. A protocol rejection before the operation is invoked MUST follow that protocol's own correlation rule.

IMP-01.statement: Dependency declarations MUST use the admitted crate, exact version, features, and default-features policy.

IMP-02.statement: The gate MUST reject every unresolved dependency, feature, source, advisory, or license disposition.

IMP-03.statement: Adapter dependency edges MUST reach the dispatcher and identity contracts and MUST NOT reach operation implementations or business storage.

IMP-04.statement: Core and operation-contract crates MUST NOT depend on protocol SDKs or generated transport types.

IMP-05.statement: Required source calls MUST be resolved by identity, and unresolved analysis MUST fail closed.

IMP-06.statement: Generated adapter output MUST equal regeneration from the admitted template and inputs.

IMP-07.statement: Scaffold MUST NOT overwrite an existing file; an existing file without a marker becomes merge-required.

IMP-08.statement: Template bodies MUST NOT be delivered by context; only rule text, contract tables, and template references are delivered.

IMP-09.statement: Missing implementation reports, missing tests, zero selected tests, and failed detectors MUST NOT pass.

IMP-10.statement: Every project MUST pin the law spec_version, dist hash, and policy hash; a mismatch fails unless a scoped exception exists.

IMP-11.statement: Every implementation rule MUST have a detector or an explicit attestation row.

IMP-12.statement: Pipeline checkpoints MUST invoke template, implementation-check, gate, and attest through a bounded wrapper.

INV-06.statement: Conformance tests, not documentation, prove compliance.

MCP-01.statement: Every applicable catalog operation has one MCP tool.

MCP-02.statement: The tool name is `operation_id` with `.` replaced by `_`, optionally prefixed.

MCP-03.statement: The tool input schema is generated from the operation request.

MCP-04.statement: The tool output schema is generated from the operation response.

MCP-05.statement: The tool handler converts input, calls the dispatcher, and maps the result.

MCP-06.statement: The tool handler contains no business logic.

MCP-07.statement: Authorization server metadata is exposed at the configured discovery endpoint.

MCP-08.statement: Protected resource metadata identifies this MCP server as the audience.

MCP-09.statement: Unauthenticated requests receive the spec-required challenge.

MCP-10.statement: Tokens are verified by the shared `AccessTokenVerifier` with the MCP audience.

MCP-11.statement: A received token MUST NOT be passed through to a downstream API.

MCP-12.statement: The adapter does not authorize the target; the operation does.

MCP-13.statement: Every operation category has an MCP mapping.

MCP-14.statement: Error details never contain tokens, secrets, or raw provider responses.

MCP-15.statement: MCP session state lives in the adapter, not in business tables.

MCP-16.statement: Business state is read and written only through operations.

MCP-17.statement: Resource and prompt surfaces that expose business data MUST read through a query operation; adapter-owned protocol metadata is the only exception.

MCP-18.statement: Protocol errors and business execution errors are mapped separately; a protocol failure is not reported as an operation error and vice versa.

MCP-19.statement: `McpConfig` MUST record the adopted protocol version, transport profile, and capabilities, and MUST declare a binding for the selected profile that fixes operation-to-tool selection, success and failure representation, correlation location, and lifecycle mapping.

MCP-20.statement: The adapter authorizes MCP-protocol-owned resources (sessions, subscriptions) but never business resources.

MCP-21.statement: Every tool result MUST carry the operation's `request_id` in the location declared by the selected MCP binding.

MCP-22.statement: MCP adapters MUST register generated tools through the admitted rmcp tool router and MUST dispatch through the shared Dispatcher.

MCP-23.statement: Every MCP deployment MUST declare its session and replay capabilities and MUST pass cross-instance tests for those capabilities.

MCP-24.statement: MCP JSON and SSE responses MUST use SDK framing and MUST share the same tool execution path.

MCP-25.statement: Resumable MCP profiles MUST persist event cursors and MUST pass restart replay without sticky routing.

MCP-26.statement: MCP cancellation and progress MUST map to the dispatcher and MUST NOT buffer unsupported operations.

MCP-27.statement: MCP authorization MUST expose discovery and challenge, bind the configured audience, and MUST NOT pass a received token downstream.

OBS-01.statement: Logs MUST be structured and include `request_id`, `operation_id`, `subject`, result, and duration.

OBS-02.statement: Logs MUST NOT include tokens, secrets, authorization codes, or passwords.

OBS-03.statement: Metrics MUST cover operation latency, error rate, authentication failures, and audience rejections.

OBS-04.statement: Metrics and logs MUST distinguish interface, operation, and error code.

OBS-05.statement: Health endpoints MUST be minimal in public mode; detailed readiness is privileged.

OP-01.statement: Exactly one handler per operation ID.

OP-02.statement: `prepare` performs target resolution, validation, and authorization; it has no business side effect. A failed `prepare` MUST leave no replayable success result and MUST fail or release the claim.

OP-03.statement: `execute` performs reservation, mutation, commit, and outbox enqueue.

OP-04.statement: Repositories are obtained from the unit of work.

OP-06.statement: The handler does not branch on `InterfaceId`.

OP-07.statement: A handler that cannot complete uses the declared recovery policy.

OP-08.statement: Generated skeletons carry a create-once marker and are not overwritten.

OP-11.statement: Anonymous operations do not bypass rate limits or validation.

OP-12.statement: Idempotency for anonymous operations is opt-in and keyed by peer plus operation. Anonymous replay MUST be declared per operation, MUST NOT receive an authenticated context, and MUST NOT reuse the authenticated replay path.

OP-13.statement: Project operation types MUST use the types provided by `operation-contract`; a project MUST register its operations and wire them in the assembly. Shared type placement is defined by Part III.2.

OP-AUTH-01.statement: Scope is checked by the dispatcher; ownership/tenant by the authorizer.

OP-AUTH-02.statement: The authorizer uses the loaded resource, never request IDs alone.

OP-AUTH-03.statement: Cross-tenant target returns `not_found`; own target with insufficient rights returns `permission_denied`.

OP-AUTH-04.statement: Replay is authorized through `replay_authorize` against the recorded target, not through full `prepare`.

OP-AUTH-05.statement: The same identity and resource produce the same result through every interface.

OP-AUTH-06.statement: `ErasedAuthenticatedOperation` MUST expose `replay_authorize` and delegate to `Operation::replay_authorize` with the typed signature.

OP-AUTH-07.statement: Replay authorization MUST evaluate the current caller. A recorded target identifies the resource being authorized and MUST NOT be treated as evidence that the original executor was permitted.

OP-IDEM-01.statement: The namespace includes subject, tenant, and operation.

OP-IDEM-02.statement: `claim` MUST be keyed by namespace, key, canonical request hash, and lease. It MUST be atomic, MUST NOT require an authorized target, and MUST produce exactly one `Acquired` for concurrent claims.

OP-IDEM-03.statement: `same-transaction` MUST store the idempotency completion, business mutation, authorized target, and outbox intent in one business commit.

OP-IDEM-04.statement: `external` uses a lease and `recover_expired`. Its lease updates and forward recovery MUST remain distinct from `same-transaction` and MUST NOT be described as providing the same atomicity.

OP-IDEM-05.statement: A replay calls `replay_authorize` against the recorded target and never re-runs `prepare`.

OP-IDEM-06.statement: Same key + different canonical request returns `conflict`.

OP-IDEM-07.statement: Failed results are stored and replayed according to policy.

OP-IDEM-08.statement: A claim carries a generation and fencing token; `complete`, `fail`, and `renew` MUST reject a stale owner. Persistence MUST reject a commit from a stale generation or fencing token.

OP-IDEM-09.statement: For `same-transaction`, the unit of work that commits the business change MUST include idempotency completion and outbox intent in the same transaction. The dispatcher MUST NOT finalize a `same-transaction` success outside that transaction.

OP-IDEM-10.statement: External side effects carry the fencing token or an equivalent deduplication/reconciliation key.

OP-IDEM-11.statement: An in-flight claim record MAY have an undetermined authorization target. A replayable result MUST carry the target information required for re-authorization; an undetermined or placeholder target MUST NOT be stored.

OP-IDEM-12.statement: For `same-transaction`, completion MUST be owned by the unit of work and MUST NOT be performed by a synchronous `ExecutionScope::complete` or `fail` that implicitly calls the asynchronous store. An `is_completed()` post-check alone MUST NOT be treated as proof of atomicity.

OP-TX-01.statement: Repositories come from the unit of work.

OP-TX-02.statement: Outbox intent is written in the same commit as the business mutation.

OP-TX-03.statement: Publication happens after commit by a relay.

OP-TX-04.statement: The relay retries and deduplicates by `event_id`.

OP-TX-05.statement: Irreversible effects use forward recovery or isolation, not forced compensation.

OP-TX-06.statement: No unrelated external API wait occurs inside a database transaction. Database communication required by the transaction is allowed. External effects run outside the transaction or through outbox/forward recovery.

OP-TX-07.statement: A committed same-transaction result and its outbox intent MUST be recoverable after a crash. A rollback MUST leave no business change, completion result, or outbox intent.

OP-VAL-01.statement: Every request type implements the generated `ContractValidate` and is validated before the idempotency claim. Replay uses `replay_authorize` and does not call `prepare`.

OP-VAL-02.statement: Handlers MUST NOT duplicate standard input validation that the macro already generates.

OP-VAL-03.statement: Validation failures map to `invalid_input` with field, code, and English message.

OPS-01.statement: Every operation MUST have a stable `operation_id` and a typed request/response pair.

OPS-02.statement: The common invocation and result model MUST define the operation input, invocation context, correlation identifier, and success or failure meaning. Each binding MUST define its wire or CLI representation; one JSON shape MUST NOT be required for every protocol.

OPS-03.statement: `context` MAY contain `request_id`, `deadline`, `idempotency_key`, and `trace_id`. It MUST NOT contain identity, tenant, role, scope, or lease.

OPS-04.statement: `request_id` MUST be generated when absent and MUST be stable across retries of the same logical request.

OPS-05.statement: The execution pipeline MUST follow this order: decode/size → authenticate or establish anonymity → authentication requirement → scope → deadline/admission → generated input validation → idempotency claim → replay branch (`replay_authorize` then stored result) or acquire branch (`prepare` for target resolution and authorization, then `execute`) → commit/outbox → result/reply.

OPS-06.statement: No business state change or external business effect MAY occur before authorization succeeds. Execution-control metadata such as a claim MAY be recorded before authorization; a claim alone MUST NOT authorize a business change.

OPS-07.statement: Authorization MUST run inside the operation, not only in the adapter.

OPS-08.statement: Tenant and ownership MUST be derived from `VerifiedIdentity` and the target resource, never from request-supplied IDs alone.

OPS-09.statement: Mutating operations MUST define idempotency semantics: same key + same canonical request reuses the result; same key + different request returns a conflict.

OPS-10.statement: Mutations that touch multiple resources MUST use a transaction or a compensating action.

OPS-11.statement: Streaming operations MUST declare their mode and MUST define EOF, error, cancellation, and backpressure semantics.

OPS-12.statement: One operation MUST have one handler. Adapter-specific branching inside the handler is forbidden.

OPS-13.statement: Operation inputs and outputs MUST be protocol-independent. Protobuf-generated types, HTTP types, and CLI types MUST NOT appear in `*-operation`.

OPS-14.statement: An operation MUST declare `AuthenticationRequirement::Required` or `AuthenticationRequirement::Anonymous`. Anonymous is not a scope, and `Option<Identity>` or an implicit anonymous path is forbidden.

OPS-15.statement: Every operation MUST publish domain events only after commit.

OPS-16.statement: Every operation MUST have a conformance identifier and at least one oracle for normal and failure behavior.

OPS-17.statement: `ErasedPrepared` MUST be opaque: it preserves the authentication kind and operation mode, and is consumed only by the erased operation that produced it.

OPS-18.statement: The generated `ContractValidate::validate()` MUST run in the common dispatch path for every interface, before idempotency claim and business logic.

OPS-19.statement: On `ClaimOutcome::Replay` the dispatcher MUST call `replay_authorize` and MUST NOT call `prepare_validated` or `execute`; it MUST return the stored result only after authorization succeeds.

REST-02.statement: Tokens MUST NOT appear in query strings or paths.

REST-03.statement: Public and protected routers are separate; protected routes use `route_layer`.

REST-04.statement: The audience is configured per router and passed to the verifier.

REST-05.statement: All REST success replies use 200 with the semantic envelope. 201, 202, and 204 are not used; aliases use 200.

REST-06.statement: Error mapping uses the fixed category table from `Part III.2` §5.8.

REST-08.statement: Mutating requests accept `Idempotency-Key` and pass it in `WireContext`.

REST-11.statement: CORS and Origin allowlists are configured; unspecified origins are denied.

REST-12.statement: The OpenAPI document lists exactly the routes the router serves.

REST-13.statement: Aliases call the same operation; they do not contain logic.

REST-14.statement: Binary and multipart endpoints declare their media types and size limits.

REST-15.statement: Every endpoint uses the semantic envelope for requests and replies.

REST-16.statement: Aliases use the same envelope; they do not introduce a second wire shape.

REST-17.statement: Anonymous operations use the public router and `execute_anonymous`; they are not a dispatcher bypass.

REST-18.statement: The reply `request_id` is the operation's `request_id`, including on errors.

REST-19.statement: REST adapters MUST use the admitted HTTP crate and call the shared dispatcher through the adapter bridge.

REST-20.statement: Every REST rejection path MUST use the shared semantic error renderer and the canonical request_id.

REST-21.statement: OpenAPI operations and schemas MUST be generated from the same operation and validation manifest used at runtime.

SEC-01.statement: Transport MUST use TLS outside loopback-only local mode.

SEC-02.statement: Authentication endpoints and mutating operations MUST be rate-limited.

SEC-03.statement: Configuration and secrets MUST come from environment or a secret store; source code MUST NOT contain them.

SEC-04.statement: Dependencies MUST be audited for known vulnerabilities before release.

SEC-05.statement: Debug output MUST NOT leak request bodies or credentials.

SSO-01.statement: SSO MUST live in `identity-sso`. It MUST NOT be imported by `*-operation` or `*-core`.

SSO-02.statement: OIDC MUST use Authorization Code with PKCE (`S256`). Implicit grant and ROPC are forbidden.

SSO-03.statement: `state` MUST be generated per request and bound to the browser session; OIDC `nonce` MUST be used. Both MUST be single-use.

SSO-04.statement: Redirect URIs MUST be registered by exact match. Wildcards and open redirectors are forbidden.

SSO-05.statement: The external issuer (`iss`) MUST be validated per provider to prevent mix-up attacks.

SSO-06.statement: The external ID token MUST be verified inside `identity-sso` and discarded. It MUST NOT be forwarded to the API or operation layer.

SSO-07.statement: SSO output MUST be `AuthenticatedUser`; the flow MUST then call `TokenIssuer` to issue an internal access token.

SSO-08.statement: External accounts MUST be stored in `external_identities` with `UNIQUE(issuer, subject)`. Business tables MUST NOT store external provider IDs.

SSO-09.statement: Accounts MUST NOT be linked automatically by email address. Linking requires an explicit, auditable action.

SSO-10.statement: Provider client IDs and secrets MUST come from configuration or environment variables, never source code.

SSO-11.statement: Adding SSO MUST change only: the `identity-sso` crate, authentication adapters, assembly wiring, configuration, and `external_identities`. Business operations, `VerifiedIdentity`, and business tables MUST remain unchanged.

SSO-12.statement: External ID tokens and internal access tokens MUST be mutually rejected by their verification rules.

VAL-01.statement: Every request input constraint is declared once in `#[rule(...)]`.

VAL-02.statement: The macro generates the runtime validator, schema, and descriptor from the same declaration.

VAL-03.statement: Standard rules follow the conversion table in §4.

VAL-04.statement: A rule whose unit or regex dialect does not match the schema keyword MUST be emitted as a custom constraint with an explicit description, not silently converted.

VAL-05.statement: Unknown rules and rules applied to an incompatible type MUST be compile-time errors.

VAL-06.statement: Every standard and custom rule carries an `error_code`.

VAL-08.statement: Conditional rules require `when` and an English condition description.

VAL-09.statement: A custom rule without a description fails compilation.

VAL-10.statement: The runtime and the descriptor use the same `check` function and `code`.

VAL-11.statement: Adapters do not implement interface-specific input validation.

VAL-12.statement: The generated validator runs after typed conversion and before the idempotency claim; prepare runs only on the acquired branch.

VAL-13.statement: Validation failures map to `invalid_input` with field, code, and English message.

VAL-14.statement: The same input produces the same validation result through every interface.

VAL-15.statement: Every field rule appears in every applicable interface's documentation.

VAL-16.statement: Hand-written constraint lists are forbidden; documentation is generated from descriptors.

VAL-17.statement: Custom rules appear as readable English text in every interface reference, not only in an extension field.

VAL-18.statement: Validation descriptions, messages, and examples are English-only.

VAL-19.statement: Validation descriptors and generated documentation contain no secrets or sensitive examples.

VAL-20.statement: Generation is deterministic for the same descriptor set and version.

VER-01.statement: The ruleset, shared contracts, generator, and conformance kit share one version.

VER-02.statement: A project pins the version in `RULES-PROFILE.toml`.

VER-03.statement: Removing or changing a closed seam requires a major version and a migration note.

VER-04.statement: Adding an open extension point is a minor version.

VER-05.statement: Adding a rule that would reject a previously valid project requires a major version.

VER-06.statement: A rule that blocks a legitimate feature is amended by extending the seam, not by granting an exception.

WS-01.statement: The ticket is random, hashed at rest, single-use, and short-lived (30 seconds).

WS-02.statement: The ticket is bound to the subject, audience, and scopes it was issued for.

WS-03.statement: A redeemed ticket cannot be redeemed again.

WS-04.statement: The upgrade is rejected before the socket is accepted if redemption fails.

WS-05.statement: The ticket is sent in a header, never in a query parameter.

WS-06.statement: A successful upgrade is not permanent authentication.

WS-07.statement: On expiry, the server either rejects new requests and requests re-auth, or closes with a policy code.

WS-08.statement: Expired connections MUST NOT execute new operations.

WS-09.statement: Connection state transitions are explicit; illegal transitions are rejected.

WS-10.statement: Each request carries a `request_id`; the response carries the same ID.

WS-12.statement: Mutations to the same resource preserve a defined order.

WS-14.statement: The adapter calls `Dispatcher::execute_verified`; it does not call handlers directly.

WS-15.statement: Message size, frame size, queue length, and connection count are bounded.

WS-16.statement: Control queue overflow and audio queue overflow have distinct policies.

WS-17.statement: A slow reader MUST NOT block the runtime; the connection is closed with 1013.

WS-18.statement: Ping/pong intervals and timeouts are configured.

WS-19.statement: Close codes use the table above.

WS-20.statement: Disconnect cleans up connection-owned subscriptions, streams, and temporary resources.

WS-21.statement: In-flight operations may complete after disconnect; their results are discarded unless the operation is explicitly cancel-on-disconnect.

WS-22.statement: Origin allowlisting is applied before authentication.

WS-23.statement: `StreamOpen` creates a stream; the server sends `StreamItem` messages followed by exactly one `StreamEnd`.

WS-24.statement: A client stream sends `StreamItem` messages and then `StreamClose`; the server replies with `Response` or `Error`.

WS-25.statement: `StreamCancel` is idempotent, propagates to the operation, and ends with `StreamEnd::Cancelled`.

WS-26.statement: A bidi stream has independent half-close for input and output.

WS-27.statement: Backpressure applies to stream items; an overflow closes with 1013.

WS-28.statement: `stream_id` is unique per connection and is released on `StreamEnd`.

WS-29.statement: The adapter calls the dispatcher's stream methods; it does not implement business streaming.

WS-30.statement: The adapter authorizes protocol-owned subscriptions and streams against the connection identity.

WS-31.statement: The adapter MUST NOT authorize business resources; that belongs to the operation.

WS-32.statement: A subscription or stream is bound to the connection; disconnect cancels it.

WS-33.statement: Origin validation and ticket redemption MUST complete before WebSocket acceptance.

WS-34.statement: All connection queues and dispatch concurrency MUST be bounded, with overload producing the configured 1013 close path.

WS-35.statement: Stream input closure, output termination, and cancellation MUST be distinct states with deterministic cleanup.
